name: LoRA AI Image & Video Generator
tagline: Web app for training custom LoRA models and generating images and video from them without touching a GPU.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product is a friendly wrapper around open weights: Flux or SDXL for images, a video model for clips, plus a LoRA training job and a gallery. An agent can absolutely build the wrapper in an afternoon, because the interesting parts are all somebody else's code. What you cannot one-shot is the GPU: LoRA training on Flux wants serious VRAM, and video generation wants more. So the honest DIY is a local UI that either drives your own card or fans out to a rented GPU API, and at that point you have swapped a subscription for a metered bill. Fine trade if you generate a lot, worse trade if you train two LoRAs a year.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you upload 10 to 20 images, kick off a LoRA training job, then generate images and short video clips from the resulting adapter with saved prompts and a browsable output gallery.
requirements: A GPU with 24GB VRAM for local Flux LoRA training, or a fal.ai / Replicate API key to rent one
Python 3.11 and Node, or just Python if you keep the UI server-rendered
Patience for model downloads measured in tens of gigabytes
whatYouLose: Zero-setup: no CUDA versions, no diffusers pinning, no 30GB checkpoint downloads
Curated presets and sane default hyperparameters that someone already tuned for you
Whatever video model they license, which is usually the hardest piece to self-host
Fast queues and parallel jobs during the ten minutes you actually feel creative
Sharing links, hosted galleries, and a phone-friendly UI
moatNotes: The moat is renting GPUs in bulk and hiding the ugly parts, not the models. That moat evaporates the moment you own a 4090.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because training a LoRA is a chore made of tooling, not creativity. The pay-to-play version means you drag in a folder of photos, pick a preset, and get an adapter that works, instead of spending Saturday reading arguments about learning rates and network dim and why your captions ruined the likeness. Add video, where self-hosting is genuinely painful and slow, and the subscription looks reasonable for anyone whose output is measured in dozens of images rather than thousands.
notes: The UI is a weekend; the GPU is a purchase order or a metered API key.
prompt:
Build a local single-user web app called "loraforge" for training image LoRAs and generating images and short video from them. Empty folder, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud database.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI, Jinja2 templates, HTMX for interactivity. No React.
- SQLite via sqlite3 for jobs, prompts, and outputs metadata. Files on disk under ./data.
- A pluggable backend layer with exactly two implementations behind one interface: "local" (diffusers + peft for SDXL LoRA training and inference) and "remote" (fal.ai HTTP API for Flux LoRA training, image generation, and image-to-video). Choose via BACKEND env var.
- Secrets in .env, loaded with python-dotenv. FAL_KEY only, nothing else.

Features, in scope:
- Dataset page: create a dataset, upload images, auto-caption with a simple filename-derived caption plus an editable caption textarea per image, delete images.
- Train page: pick dataset, set trigger word, steps, learning rate, rank. Submit starts a background job. Show a live log tail via HTMX polling every 2 seconds.
- Job queue: one worker thread, jobs run serially, statuses queued / running / done / failed, failures store the traceback.
- Generate page: pick a trained LoRA, prompt, negative prompt, seed, steps, guidance, count. Save every output with its full parameters.
- Video: given any generated image, submit an image-to-video job through the remote backend only. If BACKEND=local, disable the button and show "local video not supported".
- Gallery: grid of outputs, filter by LoRA, click for full params, "reuse these settings" button, delete.
- Prompt library: save and reuse named prompt templates with a {trigger} placeholder.

Out of scope, do not build: users, auth, payments, sharing links, multi-GPU, cloud storage, Docker orchestration.

Deliver: requirements.txt, .env.example, a README that states VRAM requirements for the local backend honestly and how to switch to remote, and a `make run` target. Write the remote backend so it fails loudly with the exact API error text rather than swallowing it. Include three pytest tests for the job queue state machine.
